title: 给房东写信报修暖气
title_en: Asking the Landlord to Fix the Heating
summary_zh: 天冷了，暖气却不热了。Anna 给房东写了一封报修邮件：说清楚现象、已经试过的办法、哪天方便上门，还附上了视频。读完你能写一封清楚、有礼貌的报修邮件。
body: Dear Mr Hughes, I hope you are well. I am writing about the heating in the flat, which stopped working properly last Tuesday. The radiators in the living room and bedroom now stay cold even when the boiler is switched on, although the hot water is still fine. I have checked the settings and tried turning the system off and on again, as the instructions in the kitchen drawer suggest, but nothing has changed. With the nights getting colder, the flat is becoming quite uncomfortable, especially in the mornings. I am also a little worried that the walls in the bathroom are starting to feel damp. I have put a small heater in the bedroom for now, but it is not really enough for the whole flat. Could you arrange for someone to come and take a look this week? I work from home on Wednesdays and Fridays, so either of those days would be easiest, but I can also leave a key with my neighbour if another day suits the engineer better. I have attached two short videos showing the radiators and the display on the boiler, in case they help. I would be grateful if you could let me know when someone is able to come. Thank you for your help, and for sorting out the kitchen tap so quickly last month. Best wishes, Anna Kowalski

knowledge.explanation: with + 名词 + -ing 作状语，说明伴随的情况（夜里越来越冷），常用来交代原因。

speaking: 用 1 分钟练习：给房东或宿管打电话，说明家里某样东西坏了，问什么时候能来修。用上 take a look 和 in case。
writing: 用 120–150 词写一封英文邮件给房东或宿管，报修一个问题：说清楚现象、已经试过什么、你哪天方便。用一个 which 非限制性定语从句。

title: 健身房里没写出来的规矩
title_en: The Unwritten Rules of the Gym
summary_zh: 健身房的墙上没写，但老会员都懂：轮流用器械、用完擦干净、哑铃放回原处、别随便指导别人。读完你会知道这些「潜规则」背后的道理，也能用动名词主语和比较句介绍公共场所的礼仪。
body: Walk into any gym for the first time and you will notice a set of rules that nobody has written on the wall. Regulars seem to follow them without thinking, while newcomers discover them one awkward moment at a time. The most important rule is about sharing. If you are resting between sets on a machine that someone else is waiting for, it is polite to let them work in, taking turns rather than sitting there scrolling through your phone. Wiping down equipment after using it is another unspoken expectation, and in most gyms it matters more than how much you can lift. Then there is the question of space. Weights are meant to go back where they came from, because nothing annoys people more than searching the whole room for a missing pair. Standing directly in front of the mirror while someone else is trying to check their form is also considered rude, even if nobody says so. Advice is a trickier area. Some experienced members love to help, but unasked-for corrections can feel embarrassing, especially for beginners who are already nervous. The safest approach is to offer only if you see a real risk of injury, and to accept a polite no. None of these rules are difficult, and most of them come down to one idea: everyone is there to work on themselves, so make it easy for them to do that. Follow that, and the gym quickly stops feeling like a test you might fail.

knowledge.explanation: 真实条件句：if 从句用现在进行时描述当下的情况，主句给出建议。

speaking: 用 1 分钟说说：健身房、图书馆或自习室里，有哪些「没写出来的规矩」？用上 come down to 和 take turns。
writing: 用 120–150 词介绍一个公共场所的「潜规则」（如图书馆、地铁、宿舍）。用一个动名词作主语的句子和一个 nothing… more than… 的比较句。
